triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The §122 temporary-import-surcharge exemption branch fired on the witness's exemplar line flags (`if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0`), so it zeroed the 10% surcharge for every China-301-listed line regardless of origin and tied the genuine §232 carve-out to one aluminum exemplar row, whereas the cited proclamation excludes only the Annex I/II product categories and articles subject to §232 restrictions.

triage.verifier_justification: I tried and failed to refute this. The §122 exemption condition is a formula change, not a rename or provenance edit: the same commit re-binds `entry_is_line_a` to `entry_is_china_301_list123` and `entry_is_line_b` to `entry_is_section_232_aluminum` / `entry_is_china_301_2024_action` in the neighbouring §301 and §232 rules, so one caller input had been serving as three unrelated legal memberships and the §122 zero fired on China-301 list membership for any origin. Read at the pinned release, Proclamation 11012 grounds only two exclusions — ¶(2) "shall not apply to imports of articles listed in paragraph 2 of Annex I ... and as enumerated in Annex II" and ¶(4) "shall not apply in addition to tariffs imposed under section 232" — and contains no §301-list-based exclusion, so the pre-fix condition had no basis in the cited source and the fix re-grounds it on exactly those two predicates, which is untraceable_branch rather than a missing clause or a polarity error. The §122 proof atoms are byte-identical pre and post, which rules out the mechanical (excerpt/citation-string) reading.

triage.verifier_notes:
Strongest surviving counter-argument, worth a reviewer's eye: the unchanged proof atoms already cite the right exclusions (chapter-99 page-221 subdivision (aa)(ii), page-226 excerpt "7202.11.10", page-230 "articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper..."), and the two exemplar lines the old flags named — 7202.11.10.00 (ferroalloy, on the §122 annex list) and 7601.10.30.00 (aluminum, §232-covered) — are genuinely exempt. So on the five-line hand-built witness the old branch gave right answers by line identity; it is wrong only because these generated chapter-scale modules document the flags as "caller inputs supplied by entry preparation from incidence classification" and run over every line in the chapter. The defect is therefore scale-dependent, but it is within the module's claimed scope (schedule_statutory_stack over chNN_general_rate[hts_line]) and the maintainers themselves call the old behavior unlawful and enumerate 18 witness-slice cells that changed. Second-best kind if a reviewer disagrees: wrong_entity_or_scope (the exemption applied to the wrong population of articles).

Three further caveats: (1) This module diff bundles several distinct fidelity changes — the quoted §122 re-grounding, per-list §301 gating, and Brazil/forced-labor gates that both drop the a/b suppression and ADD a list-membership condition (that pair reads closer to unrepresented_clause). It also adds `section_232_steel_component_rate` plus a new `+ section_232_steel_component_rate` stack term, which is new coverage the module never claimed (the witness has no steel slot) and should not be scored as the defect. Keep the §122 line as the case's anchor. (2) The identical generated change lands in all 100 chapter modules of commit a9562cfd44, so the corpus likely holds ~100 near-duplicate instances of this one defect; dedupe before using them as independent cases. (3) The fix is partial: `entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded: entry_is_line_a` and `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded: entry_is_line_b` still stand in the post file, so the exemplar-proxy pattern remains live for the reciprocal IEEPA components.

Read-only commands used; nothing in rulespec-us or the corpus was modified. Source verified through the pinned release us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap (corpus commit e79781bd), provision us/rulemaking/federal-register/2026-02-25/2026-03824.
